answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and registers on the public tide board, which assigns a spiral index k. Fees follow a quadratic spiral: the kth identity pays twice k squared, so the 1000th pays 2,000,000; 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 667,667,000, and registrations send a ripple through later prices. Registration is key-bound: the board rejects duplicates under one key, and auditors recompute fees from the index. A rented-registration ring fails: rented keys pay their quadratic fee and cannot share registration. An honest agent pays 70 plus 2 once, refunded if clean.
